title: Outposts

D0.outcome: Explains an outpost as a piece on an advanced square that no enemy pawn can attack, usually supported by a pawn, with an open file or key squares behind it.

D1.outcome: Places a knight on a named outpost square and names the pawn that supports it and the squares it eyes.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, says whether a square is a real outpost for a named piece by checking the supporting pawn and that no enemy pawn can expel the piece.

D3.outcome: Predicts the effect of one-feature changes (the supporting pawn on e3 instead of e4; a lever that can dislodge the knight) and decides whether to trade the outpost piece.

misconceptions: A knight on the fifth rank is automatically an outpost.
An outpost is strong whatever the pawn structure behind it.
conditions: A protecting pawn is present, there is an open file or squares behind, and the opponent cannot kick the piece with a pawn without damage.
Its strength comes from its hinterland: remove the supporting pawn or the open file and it loses its point.
contrasts: Knight on d5 with the supporting pawn on e3 instead of e4, so the square is no longer a weakness for the enemy.
The enemy can expel the knight with a pawn lever.
The outpost has no useful targets from its square.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.CENTER.CONTROL.D1: an outpost chain starts from the centre
